newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel propaganda drive before Mobutu return.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel propaganda drive before Mobutu return.

text.p: Zairean rebels on Monday appealed to government troops to switch sides and join their forces, renewing a propaganda war designed to weaken army morale ahead of President Mobutu Sese Seko's return home.
The appeal was issued in two documents signed by two lieutenant-colonels in the Zairean army who have apparently switched sides and joined the rebels.
The documents were obtained by Reuters from senior aides to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, president of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (ADFL).
"It is I, Lieutenant-Colonel Joseph Alidor Siku Tchomba. I call on all members of the Zairean army to join the Congo Liberation Army (ALC) so as to serve our nation," one said.

"I am addressing you today, to ask you to lay down your arms and join the ranks of the ALC in order to improve the lives of men, women and children in our dear country," said a second seven-page document signed by Lieutenant-Colonel, Technician and Chief of Staff, Lokilo Nene Boseka.
Both documents gave detailed career biographies of the soldiers' rise through Zairean army ranks but said nothing about why they switched sides. The two soldiers were little known.

Tchomba said that indiscipline in the army was caused by non-payments, division, tribalism, non-respect for the hierarchy and the chief of the Zairean army himself. He gave no details on how the Zairean army chief caused indiscipline.
Zairean rebels, who declared a ceasefire and proposed negotiations last week, control much of north and south Kivu after a two-month campaign against the Zairean army.
Zairean government forces, weakened by indiscipline and low morale, collapsed before the rebel advances at Goma, Bukavu and Uvira and the army fled, looting heavily, witnesses said.
Goma residents say the defeat of the army in November has ended the tyranny of Zairean government soldiers in the town.
Mobutu plans to return on Tuesday after six weeks convalescing on the French Riviera from cancer surgery, one of his sons said.
"He will be leaving on Tuesday morning and fly to Kinshasa," Mobutu Nzanga told Reuters on Sunday from Roquebrune-cap-Martin where Mobutu is staying in a mansion overlooking the Mediterranean.
He said the president, who has ruled for 30 years, would take off from Nice airport between 7.30 a.m. and 9 a.m. (0630 and 0800 GMT) and make a speech in Kinshasa.

In his absence, Kabila's troops took control of a swath of territory about 500 km (300 miles) long in eastern Zaire, displacing hundreds of thousands of refugees from neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi, many of whom have since returned home.
Zairean forces still control the key towns of Kisangani, Walikale and Kindu and were bringing in reinforcements, according to aid workers.

"The rebels have control of south Kivu and north Kivu up to around Fizi, but the question is how far they are prepared to go and what kind of response Kinshasa will offer," a senior aid worker told Reuters in Goma on Sunday.
The rebels made no comment on Mobutu's planned return.
